title: Roles
intro: A role groups capabilities, which are permissions for specific actions. Assign roles to people in Users. The Users sheet assigns one role per person.
Use your own role names and access requirements. The pictures show a temporary Documentation reader role in an isolated test installation. No practice data is required.

You need View roles to inspect roles, and Manage roles to create, change, delete or assign them. Opening Users also requires View users. Creating or editing identity details requires Manage users. Administrator is locked. Other system roles can be edited, but cannot be deleted.
For installation and command-line setup, read Start here. This preview covers the Roles page.

tasks.title: Inspect a role before changing access
intro: Use this to check which actions an existing role grants.
steps: Open your user menu at the bottom left, choose Settings, then select Roles.
Select a role row. Read its name, description and selected capabilities. Scroll the sheet to read each permission.
The built-in Administrator displays a warning and read-only fields. Select Close at the top right when finished.
tasks.result: Reading a role does not change its permissions.

tasks.title: Create a role with selected permissions
intro: Use this when existing roles do not match the access your staff need. Decide the required actions before selecting capabilities.
steps: Select the dots above the Roles table.
Use a name your team recognises. The example uses Documentation reader.
The Slug is the role identifier. The name fills it automatically until you edit it. Choose it carefully because you cannot change it after creation.
Enter its purpose in Description. This helps other administrators understand who should receive it.
Turn on each permission the role needs. Read the description beside each switch. The example selects View dashboards.
Select the dots at the top of the Create role sheet.
tasks.result: The sheet closes and the role appears in the list. Creating a role does not assign it to anyone. Use Users to assign it.

tasks.title: Change a role description or permissions
intro: Use this when the responsibilities of people holding a role change. Check who holds it before changing access.
steps: Enter its name in Search roles. The example searches Documentation.
Select the dots on the matching role row.
Select Edit. Selecting the row opens the same sheet.
Change Description if its purpose has changed. You may also change Name. Slug stays read-only.
Turn capabilities on or off. The example adds View reports.
Open the sheet dots and select Save.
tasks.result: The list shows the saved description. Users assigned this role receive its permissions.

tasks.title: Delete a custom role
intro: Use this only when people should lose the permissions this role grants. System roles cannot be deleted.
steps: Find the role and open its row dots. Select Delete.
Read the confirmation. Members lose the capabilities granted by this role. Select Delete to confirm, or Cancel to keep it.
tasks.result: The role disappears. Deletion cannot be undone. Check affected users after removing a role.

tasks.title: Inspect roles on a phone
intro: Use the same Roles page on a phone. Wide table columns can require horizontal scrolling.
steps: Select the role row. Scroll the sheet to read its description and capabilities. Select Close at the top right to return.

end.title: Optional practice
paragraphs: In a test installation, follow Create a role using Documentation reader. Select only View dashboards. Add View reports in the edit task, then delete the practice role when finished. Do not assign the practice role to real staff.

end.title: Before changing access
paragraphs: Administrator is locked. Other system roles can be edited but cannot be deleted. A saved slug cannot be changed.
Creating a role does not assign it to anyone. Role assignments are managed on Users. Check the people affected before changing or deleting an assigned role.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: The role is read-only. Check whether you opened the locked Administrator role and whether your account has Manage roles.
A new role does not change anyone's access. Creating the role only stores its permissions. Use Users to assign the role to the intended person.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Start here explains the installed and development CLI. Users covers assigning roles to people.
